title: Demonstrationes circa residua ex divisione potestatum per numeros primos resultantia

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E449 proves the 'supplementary' quadratic-residue facts for -1, +2, -2 (and earlier ±3) using Fermat-style descent instead of quadratic reciprocity.

End of Coroll. 3 (§89). The previous pages showed two facts. First, +2 is a non-residue for primes p ≡ ±3 (mod 8), by descent on the form 2p²−q². Second, -1 is a residue for p ≡ 1 (mod 4). For p ≡ 5 (mod 8) the product of a residue (-1) and a non-residue (+2) is a non-residue, so -2 is also a non-residue. Hence no prime 8m−3 ever divides 2p²+q² or 2p²−q² with gcd(p,q)=1.

Scholion 1 (§90): a second descent, on x²+2y².
- Claim: a coprime value N = 2p²+q² is never divisible by a prime d ≡ 5 or 7 (mod 8).
- Residues of N: with q odd, N ≡ 1 or 3 (mod 8). If q is even, N is twice a value of the same form, so one may pass to q odd.
- Reduction: given such a d, reduce p and q mod d to absolute values below d/2. Then 2p²+q² = d·k with k < d.
- Euler's 'quoti eiusdem forent formae': since N ≡ 1,3 and d ≡ 5,7 (mod 8), k ≡ 5 or 7 (mod 8). For example 1·5⁻¹ ≡ 5 and 3·5⁻¹ ≡ 7. So k has a prime factor d' < d of the bad classes, and d' divides a smaller coprime value of the form.
- Descent bottom: this ends at 5 or 7. Neither divides a coprime 2p²+q², because -2 is a non-residue mod 5 and mod 7.
- Conclusion: -2 is a non-residue for p ≡ 5,7 (mod 8). Combining with (−1/p) = −1 for p ≡ 7 (mod 8) gives +2 a residue for p ≡ 7 (mod 8). For p ≡ 5 (mod 8), +2 is a non-residue, consistent with §89.

The gap Euler admits: he says that for p ≡ 1 (mod 8), proving both +2 and -2 are residues 'can hardly be shown by similar reasoning'. Descent only proves non-divisibility, i.e. non-residuacity.

Scholion 2 (§91) introduces the summary table on the next page: ±1, ±2, ±3 classified by p mod 4, 8, 12. The table then continues by induction to ±5 mod 20, which is effectively the empirical statement of quadratic reciprocity.

Purpose: to establish the second supplementary law and its companion for -2, and to derive Fermat's theorem p = 2a²+b² for p ≡ 3 (mod 8) (§88).
errors: No real error. The phrase 'quoti eiusdem forent formae' is elliptic. Read literally ('the quotient is of the form 2pp+qq') it would need an unproved division lemma. What the argument actually needs is that the quotient is ≡ 5 or 7 (mod 8) and hence has a smaller prime factor of the bad type, which is true.
The reduction to coprime p, q with q odd after reducing mod d (removing common factors < d, handling even q) is tacit but routine.

ideas.what: -2 is a non-residue of primes ≡ 5,7 (mod 8), proved by infinite descent on prime divisors of x²+2y²
ideas.modern_name: Supplementary law for (−2/p), non-residue half; descent on the norm form of Z[√−2]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (descent proofs of 1750s–1770s); Lagrange 1775 Recherches d'arithmétique
ideas.where_published: E449 (Novi Comm. 18); similar descent arguments appear in Euler's earlier papers on divisors of forms (e.g. E256 and related), details unsure

ideas.what: +2 is a residue for p ≡ 7 (mod 8) and a non-residue for p ≡ 5 (mod 8), via multiplicativity of the residue character with (−1/p)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler / Lagrange; full proof including 8n+1 by Lagrange and Euler, and Gauss (Disquisitiones art. 112–116)

ideas.what: Explicit admission that the case p ≡ 1 (mod 8) (±2 residues) is not reachable by the descent method
ideas.modern_name: Case p ≡ 1 (mod 8) of the 2-supplement, later handled e.g. by (x + x⁻¹)² = 2 for x⁴ ≡ −1, or by Gauss's arguments
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (later, Opuscula analytica era, unsure of exact paper), Lagrange, Gauss
ideas.where_published: this page; resolution in later works (exact Euler reference unsure)

ideas.what: Summary table of residuacity of ±1, ±2, ±3 by prime class, extended by induction to ±5

deep.surprise_reason: Standard, well-documented material: the descent proof of the supplementary law for ±2 and the known limitation at p ≡ 1 (mod 8), which historians (Weil, Lemmermeyer) discuss. Nothing new.
